chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said:
Aḥmad ibn al-Nuʿmān asked and said: “May I perform salat (prayer) in my litter while I am ill?” He said: “As for the supererogatory prayer, yes; but as for the obligatory prayer, no.”

And Aḥmad mentioned the severity of his pain, so he said: “I had been severely ill, and when the time of salat (prayer) came, I would order them to make me stand, and I would be carried on my bedding and set down, and I would perform salat (prayer), then I would be carried on my bedding and placed in my litter.”

So this narration is to be understood as referring to a kind of recommendation, or to a condition in which one is able to be lowered to the ground. Salat (prayer) in the litter is only permissible when one is unable to get down, in a manner indicated by that.

key_terms.النُّزُولِ: descending from the mount or litter

ai.seo_question: Can a sick person perform obligatory salat (prayer) in a litter or while mounted?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) in a litter for a sick traveler. It distinguishes between supererogatory prayer, which is allowed in the litter, and obligatory prayer, which is not allowed unless the person is unable to descend, indicating a legal concession based on incapacity.
